title: Dental PPO Plans Benefit Computation for a Reprocessed Initial-Wait Line
content:
Claims computation standard, Dental PPO Plans: the plan payment and patient share of a line reprocessed after a denial for the waiting period counted from the coverage effective date (a reprocessed initial-wait line).

## 1. Inputs
All facts are those of the denied line: its service class, procedure, tooth, extraction date, date of service, benefit year, billed amount, allowed amount, network status and the primary payment recorded on it by another carrier. Plan figures (waiting periods, missing-tooth clause months, individual deductible and its preventive waiver, in-network coinsurance, annual maximum, secondary payment method) are those of the enrollment's plan in the Dental PPO Plans schedules.

## 2. Formal clause
**2.1 Allowance and coinsurance.** The payment on a reprocessed initial-wait line is figured on the line's allowed amount. The coinsurance is the plan's in-network percentage for the line's service class.

**2.2 Waiting-period test.** The line is payable only when its date of service is at least its waiting period counted in whole calendar months from the coverage effective date. A month counts as whole when the day of the month of the date of service is not earlier than that of the coverage effective date, which always falls on the first of a month. The waiting period is the one for the line's service class that applies to the enrollment: the plan's individual waiting period for individual and individual exchange enrollments, its late-entrant waiting period for group enrollments of a late entrant, and none for other group enrollments or for preventive services. Otherwise the plan payment is 0.00.

**2.3 Missing-tooth test.** When the plan's missing-tooth clause months are above 0, a line for a bridge, denture or implant that replaces a tooth whose extraction date is before the coverage effective date is payable only once the months of continuous enrollment, counted in whole calendar months from the coverage effective date to the date of service, reach the clause months. The clause does not apply to group enrollments entered at open enrollment, as new hires or by special enrollment. A line the clause still bars has a plan payment of 0.00.

**2.4 Deductible.** The deductible taken is the plan's individual deductible less the person's deductible postings net of deductible reversals for the line's benefit year, never below zero and never more than the allowance the payment is figured on. A preventive-class line on a plan that waives the preventive deductible, or any line on a plan whose individual deductible is 0.00, takes none. Because every Cascade plan's family deductible maximum is three times its individual deductible, on an account with no more than three enrolled persons the family limit never falls below the person's own remaining deductible, so the line counts only the person's own deductible postings.

**2.5 Normal benefit and rounding.** The normal benefit is the allowance less the deductible taken, times the coinsurance, rounded to the cent with a half cent rounded up. The plan payment and patient share are rounded to the cent the same way.

**2.6 Other carrier.** The other-carrier adjustment follows the plan's secondary payment method and the primary payment recorded on the denied line: with non-duplication the normal benefit is reduced by that payment, never below zero; with standard coordination of benefits the payment is limited to the allowed amount less that payment; when no primary payment is recorded no adjustment is made.

**2.7 Annual maximum.** The plan payment is never more than the person's remaining annual maximum for the line's benefit year: the plan's annual maximum less the person's maximum postings net of maximum reversals for that benefit year.

**2.8 Patient share.** The patient share is the billed amount less the plan payment for a line from an out-of-network practice, and the allowed amount less the plan payment otherwise, never below zero.

**2.9 Order.** The waiting-period and missing-tooth tests come first; then the allowance and coinsurance give the normal benefit; then the other-carrier deduction, never taking the payment below zero; then the other-carrier ceiling; then the annual-maximum ceiling, which gives the plan payment. The patient share is figured last from the plan payment, its zero floor last.

## 3. Worked example (hypothetical figures)
In-network basic-class filling on an individual enrollment, coverage effective 1 February, date of service 9 August, plan individual basic waiting period 6 months, individual deductible 50.00 with 21.00 already posted (net) for the year, in-network basic coinsurance 80 percent, annual maximum 1250.00 with 611.35 posted (net), non-duplication, no primary payment. Allowed amount 263.90; billed amount 301.00.
- Whole months from 1 February to 9 August: 6, so the line is payable.
- Deductible taken: 50.00 less 21.00, which is 29.00.
- Normal benefit: 263.90 less 29.00 is 234.90; times 80 percent is 187.92.
- Remaining annual maximum: 1250.00 less 611.35, which is 638.65; the plan payment is 187.92.
- Patient share: 263.90 less 187.92, which is 75.98.

Had the date of service been 31 July, only 5 whole months would have run: the plan payment would be 0.00 and the patient share 263.90.
